sections.html:
• Common names: Common Pleco, L021, L023, Albino pleco
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC) (IUCN 2023)
In Southeast Asia they are bred in large numbers, so wild-caught fish are only rarely traded. All the more beautiful is it to obtain some splendidly marked wild-caught juveniles.
Liposarcus pardalis has an enormous area of origin that encloses nearly the entire Amazon basin.
South America: Lower, middle and upper Amazon River basin. Introduced to countries outside its native range.
It is found in different water types.
Grows too large for the majority of home aquariums so would need to be housed in a 180 cm (6 ft) tank or over. Can be housed with most large fish due to its robust nature.
Because it is found in different water types, it is highly adaptable for keeping in aquaria.
Given its size (over 40 cm), enormous quantities of food are consumed.
Omnivore, vegetable and meaty foods plus flake, tablet and pellet foods. Will eat algae when young but not so much when it gets older.

Given two L-numbers in the past, L021 and L023. Part of the P. multiradiatus group due to the lack of the hump on the head which relates to the P. lituratus group. The genus name has now been reclassified back to Pterygoplichthys from Liposarcus due to the work carried out by J.W. Armbruster 2004. There are still some publications that still use Liposarcus as the preferred genus name.

Pterygoplichthys species can be differentiated from the Hypostomus group by the larger amount of dorsal fin rays, which is usually over 10. This is probably why it has been miss sold many times as Hypostomus plecostomus in the hobby.

Albino varieties first arrived in the U.K. in the early nineties through breeding programs carried out in the Czech Republic and it is now a common species bred in the fish farms of the Far East and also Florida in the United States. This species has also been introduced in the Philippines alongside P. disjunctivus probably from unwanted aquarium specimens.

Etymology: The specific name pardalis: párdalis, leopard, referring to round leopard-like spots or points of dark brown on a light-yellow background.
